guides.favoredWhen: Irelia wins by baiting Counter Strike and fighting fully stacked; Jax wins if he dodges the stun and denies her resets.

keyTips.text: Set up minions to dash through before trading. Prepared Q targets give you entry and exit; without them, never start the exchange.
keyTips.heading: Dash setup

keyTips.text: Bait Counter Strike, then commit. Feint a dash to draw E, and take the real trade only once the shield is down.
keyTips.heading: Bait first

keyTips.text: All-in after he misuses E. The wasted shield is your window, so convert it immediately instead of resetting to neutral.
keyTips.heading: Punish window

tips.text: Stagger the stun because he holds E for it. Never throw E on pattern; vary the moment so his shield guesses fail.
tips.heading: Stun timing

tips.text: Keep the passive stacked to zone him. He tracks your stacks to decide trades, so a stacked wave holds him off without fighting.
tips.heading: Stack pressure

tips.text: Keep an exit minion behind you. Every committed dash needs a way back, so fight on your prepared side of the wave.
tips.heading: Exit discipline

tips.text: Vary dash targets because he counts resets. Dashing the same minion twice lets him time the stun; spread the chain across the wave.
tips.heading: Dash variety

tips.text: Fight fully stacked and finish before E returns. The stacked all-in outdamages him, but only inside the shield downtime.
tips.heading: Stacked finish

tips.text: Never dash into a held Counter Strike when stacked. Losing full stacks to the stun reverses the lane, so wait out the shield first.
tips.heading: Shield respect

guides.favoredWhen: Skill lane, slightly hers. Stack freely, mark her dashes, never let shroud waste marks.

keyTips.text: Skill lane, slightly hers: respect her anyway, outscale stacks.
She Qs when you Q a minion, careful at 3+ stacks: your farm is her poke, so farm stacked.
She never bursts into your W: the wall eats her combo, so hold it.

tips.text: She dodges your stun with MS, E or R: the mark never lands clean, so layer it.
She respects stacked waves: 3+ stacks means she backs off, so stack.
She waits out marks in shroud: marked time is hidden time, so hold the Q.
Your Q onto her invites her E: E first, Q after.
Stacks kept plus Ws held: the Akali who never answers never wins.

sources.author: Anguish333
sources.rankClaim: Master (profile badge; title claims 2000LP GrandMaster EUW and Challenger EUNE) · Akali main

guides.favoredWhen: Irelia wins PTA plus Ignite all-ins when Riposte is down; Fiora wins if W answers the ultimate and she controls level 1.

keyTips.text: Take Press the Attack with Ignite. The setup turns your stacked all-ins lethal, which is the only exchange pattern that beats her dueling.
keyTips.heading: Setup

keyTips.text: Never give her an obvious E. Riposte answers predictable stuns, so stagger the cast and force her to guess.
keyTips.heading: Stun discipline

keyTips.text: Expect level-1 minion denial and the alcove ambush. She zones you off the wave and waits around corners, so path wide and concede what you must.
keyTips.heading: Level-1 respect

tips.text: Stagger Q instead of dashing on pattern. She holds her Q until you spend yours, so threaten without committing and dash only on your terms.
tips.heading: Dash patience

tips.text: Time E for after her Q-step, not before. Dashing into her held Q hands her the trade; answer the step-in instead of opening into it.
tips.heading: Answer, don't open

tips.text: Commit the ultimate only when Riposte is down. She saves W for R above all, so the full combo needs the parry spent first.
tips.heading: Ult timing

tips.text: Dash to minions, not to her. She follows your dash to punish the landing, so chain through the wave and strike from its cover.
tips.heading: Wave cover

tips.text: Take stacked all-ins inside the W downtime. With Riposte spent, your PTA plus Ignite pattern outdamages her answerless dueling.
tips.heading: All-in window

tips.text: Hold R as the finisher once W is gone. The blades land clean without the parry threat, closing the stacked fight she cannot leave.
tips.heading: Finisher

itemization.text: Take Ignite over Teleport, with early Executioner's Calling only when skipping Ignite. The lane is decided by all-in lethality, not sustain.

guides.favoredWhen: Irelia wins by punishing missed Decimates and converting the level 4–5 and Blade of the Ruined King windows; Darius wins if he denies early XP, dodges the stun, and reaches Shojin stacks.

keyTips.text: Punish him after he misses Decimate. The whiffed Q is your entry: step in while it is down instead of waiting for the next cast.
keyTips.heading: Punish window

keyTips.text: Take favorable fights at levels 4–5. That is your early peak against him, before his later scaling answers take over the lane.
keyTips.heading: Timing window

keyTips.text: Never chase him through minions; sidestep Apprehend. He chains Q off your dashes, so vary your dash targets and break the stun line instead of running it straight.
keyTips.heading: Stun discipline

tips.text: Do not concede the level-1 XP zone. He wants to deny you before your passive stacks, so hold minion contact and stack on the wave before trading.
tips.heading: Level 1

tips.text: Approach from angles his E cannot cover. Chain Q through different minions on each trade so his pull guesses fail and his Q edge never catches the full dash.
tips.heading: Dash angles

tips.text: After level 6, lead with the R slow into E. He fears walking into your ultimate because the slow sets up the stun, so cast R first and land E on the slowed target.
tips.heading: Post-6 combo

tips.text: Rush Blade of the Ruined King to punish every missed dodge. Each Q he fails to land gets more costly once the item is done, so force all-ins instead of farming it out.
tips.heading: First item

tips.text: Beat him to the item turn. His Bramble Vest plus Steelcaps window answers your rush, so complete Blade of the Ruined King first and run him down before his armor stack lands.
tips.heading: Item race

tips.text: End fights before five stacks once Spear of Shojin is done. After that spike he looks for five stacks into the ultimate, so take short all-ins and never offer the extended brawl.
tips.heading: Post-Shojin rule

itemization.text: Build Blade of the Ruined King first for the all-in turn, since the matchup swings on that spike more than on any rune choice.

guides.favoredWhen: You dominate lane and side. She keeps the wave close and holds E. Break it, snowball.

keyTips.text: You dominate lane and side: snowball to matter, denial is defeat.
She respects your level 2 and 6 all-ins: the spikes are lethal, so force them.
She holds E to break your trades: the stun is her exit, so bait it.

tips.text: She concedes gold for HP: zone her off both.
She takes Bone Plating and plays safe to blunt your spikes, so stack through.
She keeps the wave on her side for ganks: break it, crash and dive with yours.
She stays away from low-HP minions: your Q reset starts there, so farm low.
Snowballed plus unstoppable: the Syndra whose E never exits you never stops you.

guides.favoredWhen: Rarely killable for him. He plays for timers, not the duel. Stack on the wave, hold E.

keyTips.text: You are rarely killable: he plays for timers, not the solo kill.
He stays off the wave and away from casters: your Q resets on minions to reach him, so push.
He trades only with Bone Plating up or Ignite ready: without one you out-trade, so force.

early-lane.text: Zed often places Living Shadow before Death Mark so he can swap away from skillshots. Hold your crowd control until he has used the swap.

win-condition.text: Death Mark always lands Zed behind his target. Pre-aim crowd control and escapes behind you, not toward where he cast it.

tips.text: He pokes, never commits: short shadow Qs are his whole plan, so heal through.
He concedes CS to keep HP: his health is for jungle plays, so zone him off gold.
Death Mark always lands Zed behind his target. Pre-aim crowd control and escapes behind you, not toward where he cast it.
His R dodges your E or removes your Q mark: hold E until after shadows.
Duel decided, wave watched: roams and jungle setups never save him.

keyTips.text: Play AP Irelia as a mid-to-late scaler with explosive area damage across W, E, and R.
Value passive stacks in lane and early fights on both the AP and auto-attack builds.
Zone or catch several opponents with R, parking the main target where follow-up damage lands.

tips.text: Reposition through targets with Q, keeping resets alive when other damage kills the target mid-dash.
Absorb AP dives behind Defiant Dance, whose reduction climbs steeply with AP.
Read W offense as physical and weaker into heavy armor, holding it as defense there instead.
Stun groups with E, delaying the second blade and opening from out of vision to hide the setup.
After a confirmed E stun, charge W at once and follow with R near peak charge.
Reposition through fights with Q, resetting on E, R, or low-health targets to keep an exit open.
Engage post-6 with E into W into R, releasing W near its mid-charge damage peak instead of full-holding.
Start R onto targets without Flash, letting its slow set up the E follow.
When outnumbered, back out through the ultimate area so pursuers eat its damage.
Thread E across multiple enemies for squishy threats, since the AP build exists for area burst.
Land skillshots before committing, since the build leans on them with few escapes.
Treat W as a defensive cooldown too, with real squishiness underneath it.
Spend the AP burst window directly, saving the auto-attack build for lanes that allow a free split plan.

itemization.text: Prioritize AP first, then cooldown reduction, sustain and utility, health, magic penetration, and defense in that order.
Run Electrocute with Sudden Impact, Grisly Mementos, and Ultimate Hunter plus Manaflow Band and Transcendence, with Flash and Teleport as the safe spells.
Call Blackfire Torch the highest-damage AP route, Malignance the long-range initiation pick into squishy ranged teams or beside divers, and Lich Bane the melee-target answer.
Build Hextech Gunblade first or second for sustain and burst, with Lich Bane, Hextech Rocketbelt, Rabadon's Deathcap, and Cryptbloom as options.
Take Rocketbelt second against spell shields that eat poke, valuing its extra dash with no Q target around.
Buy Liandry's Torment into health stackers since W, E, R, and Q all apply it, and Rabadon's Deathcap third while ahead or into attack-heavy teams.

keyTips.text: Stack the passive to four before isolated duels; without a wave or stacks, the 1v1 collapses.
Peak through early-to-mid game and spend item and level leads on skirmishes there.
Respect crowd-control-heavy and high-armor teams that stall her movement and damage.

tips.text: Track Q damage each rank; a minion left alive breaks the reset and strands Irelia.
Prep low-health minions with W for clean Q resets.
Keep a wave around before fighting, since R plus W can clear it and erase the next Q targets.
Q to a minion and cast E with the cursor held on it to hide the first blade animation.
Open E1 and hold E2 to force reactions under pressure.
Cast R before E when possible so the blade field cuts escape paths and lands E easier.
Build stacks fast with E, W, Q, Q when no wave can supply them.
At level 9, learn the max-rank Q plus Blade of the Ruined King backline threshold so resets never drop.
Escape through Q on nearby minions or jungle monsters when no champion target stays safe.
Hold a minion wave before engaging so Q keeps resetting and carrying mobility through the fight.
Constrain movement with R into E, then chain Q across marked targets.
Play carefully into difficult control and armor teams.
Win extended fights on wave access plus four stacks, refusing stack-less isolated duels.
Lock targets with R and E for the teamfight follow-up instead of entering with no wave or reset path.
Flee bad fights on Q hops across nearby minions or camps.

itemization.text: Run Conqueror with Triumph, Legend: Alacrity, and Last Stand plus Bone Plating and Unflinching.
Swap Resolve to Second Wind and Overgrowth into ranged opponents.
Take Flash and Teleport for top lane.
Rush Blade of the Ruined King first, pairing it with Terminus and Hullbreaker in the common build.

Add Wit's End into AP threats and Mercury's Treads into heavy AP plus control; against full AD take Iceborn Gauntlet, Death's Dance, and Plated Steelcaps, and into multi-AP add Maw of Malmortius and Kaenic Rookern.
